'So the king gave the order, and they brought Daniel and threw him into the den' -- ordered by Darius, who had been manoeuvred into a decree he could not revoke and who tried until sundown to undo it (6:14).; reluctantly, having labored to save him (Dan 6:14)

'I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.' (Exod 3:6). The self-naming is by relationship to three men, before the name at 3:14. Jesus argues the resurrection out of the tense of this formula at Matt 22:32: 'God is not the God of the dead, but of the living.'
'God said to Moses, I AM WHO I AM' -- first person, and the verse names the speaker before he says it.

Implied rather than explicit precisely because of the supplied word. A reader who thinks the two are the same saying will find them one hop apart; a reader who does not will find the reason on the record.

'Before Abraham was, I am.' The KJV gives no supplied word here, unlike John 8:24, 13:19 and 18:5-6 where it reads 'I am he'. What the hearers did is in the next verse: 'they picked up stones to throw at Him.' The edge records that he said it of himself and that they reacted; it does not record what follows from either.
